transcript.content: Hello, welcome. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi. Well, I'm here because I've been having some really unsettling feelings lately. What scares me most is that... when I walk across campus, it feels like I’m watching everything through a piece of glass. It's hard to explain, but it's like I’m not fully in my own body, and the buildings and the students around me just seem slightly unreal. It's been really bothering me, so I knew I needed to come in and talk to someone.
Have you ever felt detached from yourself, as if you were observing your own thoughts or body from outside, or felt like the world around you wasn’t real?

Yeah, that's exactly what I was just trying to describe. It's... well, like I mentioned, it's that feeling of watching everything through a piece of glass. When I'm walking across campus, I just feel like I'm not totally in my own body. And the buildings and the students around me, they just seem slightly unreal. So, yes, that is exactly what I've been experiencing.
Do these feelings of detachment and unreality happen in specific situations, like when you're anxious, or do they seem to come out of the blue?

I'm not really sure, to be honest. I haven't noticed a specific pattern to it. I don't think I'm feeling particularly anxious right before it starts... it just sort of comes out of the blue. I'll just be walking to the building where I TA, and suddenly everything gets that weird, distant feeling. So, no, I haven't really been able to tie it to any specific situation or trigger.
How long do these episodes of feeling detached or like things are unreal typically last? Do they go away quickly, or do they last for a longer period of time?

I haven't really timed it, so I'm not entirely sure. It's... a little hard to gauge time when I'm feeling that way. I guess it usually just lasts for a bit while I'm walking, and then eventually things just kind of go back to normal. But I couldn't tell you if it's five minutes or twenty. It just sort of runs its course.
Have you noticed these feelings of detachment or unreality happening in situations other than when you're walking across campus, like when you're at home, in class, or doing other activities?

No, I don't think so. I haven't really noticed it happening at home or when I'm actually in the classroom teaching. It seems like it's mostly just... when I'm out walking around, like I mentioned. I haven't really felt it while I'm doing other things.
Have you ever experienced these feelings of detachment or unreality in any other situations, even briefly, like when you're alone, stressed, or just waking up?

No, I... I really don't think so. Even if I'm stressed out about grading or something, or just waking up in the morning, things feel real. It really just seems to be limited to when I'm making that walk across campus. I haven't noticed it creeping in at any other time.
Have you ever had even a brief moment where things felt even slightly unreal or you felt detached from yourself in any other situation, like while driving, reading, or talking to someone?

No, really, not while driving or reading or anything like that. Like I was saying, it's just that walk across campus. I think that's what scares me most about it, actually. When I'm walking out there, it just feels like I'm watching everything through a piece of glass... like I'm not fully in my own body, and the buildings and the students walking by are just slightly unreal. But it really is only in that specific situation. I haven't felt it anywhere else.

Have you ever experienced even a brief moment where things felt unreal or you felt detached from yourself during or after any stressful or traumatic events in your life, even if it wasn’t while walking across campus?

Um, no, honestly, I haven't. I mean, I've had stressful things happen in the past, of course, but I always felt completely present for them. I've never felt disconnected from my body or like things weren't real before. This whole feeling... it's completely new to me.

Have you ever experienced any other strange feelings related to your sense of self or reality—like feeling numb, emotionally detached, or as if you're living in a dream—especially during times of stress, even if only briefly?

No, I haven't. I know you're asking about a few different things there, but... no. I don't feel numb, and I don't feel like I'm in a dream when I'm stressed out. 

If I'm overwhelmed with my graduate work or the students I'm TAing for, it just feels like regular stress, you know? I might be tired or anxious, but I'm still fully connected to what's going on. I really haven't experienced any emotional detachment or strange reality feelings outside of that one specific walk.
Have you ever felt like you were outside of your body or watching yourself from a distance, even for a moment, during or after any particularly stressful or overwhelming experiences?

No, I haven't. Even when things have gotten really overwhelming in the past, I've never felt like I was outside of my body or watching myself from a distance. I'm always just right there in the moment.

Have you ever experienced these feelings of detachment or unreality even when you're not under any stress or in situations other than walking across campus, such as when you're relaxed or engaged in a routine task?

No, I haven't. When I'm just at home relaxing, or, you know, doing chores or something routine, everything feels completely normal. I don't get those weird detached feelings at all. Like I said, it really was just that one specific time on campus. Otherwise, I feel totally like myself.

Have you ever experienced any other symptoms along with that feeling of detachment, like changes in your vision, hearing, or a sense that time is slowing down or speeding up, while you're walking across campus?

No, nothing like that. My vision and hearing were completely normal, and time felt like it was moving at a regular pace. It was really just that strange sense of being disconnected from my surroundings, but physically, my senses were fine.
Have you ever experienced these feelings of detachment or unreality in any other specific situation in the past, even once, outside of walking across campus?

No, I haven't. It really is just that one situation. But honestly, that's what scares me the most about it. When I walk across campus, it feels like I'm watching everything through glass. It's just this strange sense that I'm not fully in my own body, and the buildings and the students around me seem slightly unreal. So, even though it hasn't happened anywhere else, going through that specific feeling there is just really disturbing to me.

Have you ever had even the slightest experience of feeling detached from yourself or that things around you felt a little unreal, even if just for a second, in any other situation—like when you're watching TV, sitting quietly, or even just thinking about something deeply?

No, really, I haven't. I know you're trying to see if there's a pattern, but it's just... it's just not there. When I'm watching TV or just sitting around, I feel completely normal. I'm fully present. It's really only that one specific situation on campus. I've never felt that weird, detached feeling any other time, not even for a second.

Have you ever, even once, felt even slightly detached from yourself or that things around you felt a little unreal when you weren’t walking across campus—like maybe right after waking up, during a quiet moment, or while deep in thought?

No, doctor, I really haven't. I know you're trying to cover all the bases here, but... no. Not when I wake up, not during quiet moments, or when I'm deep in thought. 

Like I said before, it is strictly when I'm walking across the campus. I really haven't felt that way at any other time, not even for a second.

Have you ever had any experience, even once, where you felt detached from yourself or things felt unreal in any other situation, even under extreme stress or following a trauma, even if it was just brief?

Look, I... I really don't know how else to say this. The answer is still no. 

Not under extreme stress, not after a trauma, not ever. I have never felt that way in my entire life outside of walking across that campus. That is the absolute only time it happens. I promise you, if it had happened anywhere else, I would tell you.
